text:
Not. No. Nor. But. Even don't and won't. Never, oddly enough, isn't. Now run a review through the filter. The movie was not good at all. Two words survive: movie, and good. A clearly negative review now reads like praise. So for sentiment, curate the list. Start from NLTK's, take out the words you must keep, like not, and add your own noise, like movie, in a pile of movie reviews. Run the same review again, and what survives is not good. The meaning made it through. One kind of repetition is left: one word, wearing different endings.

Run, runs, running, ran. Four forms of one word, and there are two classic ways to fold them into one. The first is stemming: chop the suffix off by rule. The best-known stemmer is Porter's, from nineteen eighty. Runs and running both come out as run. But ran stays ran. No rule knows it's the past tense. Studies and studying both become studi, with an i where the y was, and happiness becomes happi. Those aren't words at all. And organization, organize and organ all collapse into organ. That's called over-stemming. A stem is a key, not a word. That's fine, as long as you only ever compare stems with stems. The second way is to look the word up.

Lemmatizing finds a word's lemma, its dictionary form. NLTK's lemmatizer looks it up in WordNet, a database of English words. Here's the catch. By default, it treats every word as a noun. So running comes back running, ran comes back ran, and was comes back as wa. Tell it the part of speech, and it knows. As verbs, running and ran both become run, and was becomes be. As an adjective, better becomes good. No suffix rule could turn was into be. That takes knowing the word. So stem for speed, when only a machine ever sees the key, like a search index. Lemmatize when the root has to be a real word.

Look back at the four steps, and each one threw something away on purpose. The spaces. The capitals. The common words. The endings. Cleaning well means knowing what you threw away, and whether your task needed it. With the words clean, the next thing to do is count them.
